animals.name: Sri Lankan Leopard
animals.description: The Sri Lankan leopard, an apex predator and endemic subspecies, is recognized for its golden-yellow coat adorned with black rosettes and spots. Solitary and territorial, it is active both day and night, hunting a variety of prey such as deer, wild boar, and monkeys. It thrives in dry forests, grasslands, and scrublands, particularly in Yala National Park, which has one of the world’s highest leopard densities. Known for its elusive nature, it is a symbol of Sri Lanka's rich biodiversity.

animals.name: Mugger Crocodile
animals.size: Males: up to 4 meters; Females: smaller
animals.description: The mugger crocodile, also known as the marsh crocodile, is one of the most widespread crocodilian species in Sri Lanka. It thrives in freshwater environments such as lakes, rivers, and marshes. Recognized by its broad snout and dark olive-green body, it is an ambush predator, feeding on fish, birds, and mammals. Despite its fearsome reputation, it plays a vital role in maintaining wetland ecosystems. Though generally shy, human-wildlife conflicts occasionally occur near water bodies.

animals.name: Spotted Deer
animals.size: Males: up to 85 kg; Females: slightly smaller
animals.description: The spotted deer, also known as chital, is one of the most graceful and common deer species in Sri Lanka, especially in Yala National Park. Recognized by its reddish-brown coat adorned with white spots, it exhibits a striking contrast. These herbivores are highly social, often seen grazing in groups in open grasslands and forest edges. Feeding on grasses, leaves, and fruits, they play an essential role in the ecosystem. Known for their alert and swift nature, spotted deer are a primary prey for leopards in the region.

animals.name: Sri lankan Peacock
animals.size: Males: up to 2.3 meters including tail; Females: smaller
animals.description: Sri lankan Peacock is distinguished by the male’s vibrant blue-green plumage and long, iridescent tail feathers, while females are less colorful with a brownish-green appearance. Omnivorous, it feeds on seeds, fruits, insects, and small reptiles. Often found in scrublands and forest clearings, males perform elaborate courtship displays by fanning their tails. Sacred in Sri Lanka, peafowls hold cultural significance in Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

animals.name: Asian Elephant
animals.description: The Sri Lankan elephant, the largest Asian elephant subspecies, has grey skin often marked with pink patches on its ears and face. Known for their intelligence and strong social bonds, they live in matriarchal herds, while males are often solitary. They feed on grasses, leaves, fruits, and bark, requiring vast amounts of food and water daily. Found in forests, grasslands, and near water, these elephants play a crucial role in seed dispersal and ecosystem balance.

animals.name: Water Buffalo
animals.description: The water buffalo is a large, domesticated bovine species commonly found in wetlands, marshes, and grasslands of Sri Lanka. Recognized for its curved horns and dark grey to black coat, it plays an essential role in agriculture, especially in rice farming. These herbivores graze on grasses and aquatic vegetation and are known for their strong swimming abilities. Despite domestication, wild water buffalo populations still exist in Sri Lanka’s national parks, coexisting with leopards and crocodiles.

animals.name: Sri Lankan Sloth Bear
animals.description: The Sri Lankan sloth bear, a subspecies of the Indian sloth bear, is a nocturnal omnivore known for its shaggy black coat, long snout, and distinctive white chest marking. It primarily feeds on termites, ants, honey, fruits, and berries, using its strong claws to dig into termite mounds. Preferring dry forests and grasslands, it is an elusive and solitary animal, often avoiding human interaction. Due to habitat loss and declining populations, it is considered a vulnerable species in Sri Lanka.

animals.name: Sri Lankan Wild Boar
animals.size: Males: up to 150 kg; Females: smaller
animals.description: The Sri Lankan wild boar is a robust and adaptable omnivore commonly found in forests, grasslands, and wetlands. It has coarse, bristly fur ranging from dark brown to black, with prominent tusks in males. Wild boars forage for roots, fruits, insects, and small vertebrates, playing a crucial role in seed dispersal. They are social animals, living in matriarchal groups, and are a significant prey species for leopards. Though typically shy, they can be aggressive when threatened.
